content.value_statement: Teams need clear boundaries when reads and writes have different scaling needs. This skill guides CQRS design, read models, projections, and eventual consistency.
actual_capabilities: Explains command, query, event, and projector responsibilities.
Provides templates for command handlers and query handlers.
Shows FastAPI endpoint separation for commands and queries.
Covers read model synchronization from domain events.
Describes handling for stale reads and projection lag.
Lists CQRS best practices and anti-patterns.
limitations: Does not replace domain modeling or architecture review.
Does not provide production-ready database migrations.
Assumes the team can operate separate read and write models.
Requires adaptation for each framework, database, and consistency model.

use_cases.title: Plan a CQRS Refactor
use_cases.description: Map existing CRUD workflows into commands, queries, events, and read models before implementation.

use_cases.title: Design Scalable Read Paths
use_cases.description: Create read models and projection flows for reports, dashboards, and search-heavy workloads.

use_cases.title: Review Eventual Consistency
use_cases.description: Identify stale-read risks, projection recovery needs, and user-facing consistency tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Find CQRS Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a service boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my service and identify where CQRS fits. List commands, queries, read models, and consistency risks.

prompt_templates.title: Define Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Design command and query models for this workflow. Include handlers, validation rules, events, and read model fields.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Projections
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a projection strategy for these domain events. Include ordering, idempotency, replay, failure recovery, and lag monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CQRS and event sourcing review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed CQRS architecture for production risks. Cover boundaries, transactions, consistency, observability, and operational recovery.

output_examples.input: A team wants faster order reporting without slowing checkout writes.
output_examples.output: The skill can propose separate command handlers for checkout and read models for reporting. It can also flag projection lag risks.

output_examples.input: A developer needs to expose order creation and order lookup endpoints.
output_examples.output: The skill can outline separate command and query endpoints, then describe handler responsibilities and read model access.

output_examples.input: An architect wants to add event sourcing to a CQRS system.
output_examples.output: The skill can describe event storage, projection replay, idempotent projectors, and stale-read handling.

best_practices: Start with clear read and write workload differences.
Design projections to be idempotent and replayable.
Make eventual consistency visible in product behavior and operations.
anti_patterns: Do not add CQRS to simple CRUD domains without scale or model pressure.
Do not share write-model internals directly with read queries.
Do not ignore projection lag, replay failures, or stale data warnings.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design CQRS systems with command handlers, query handlers, read models, projections, and consistency handling.

faq.question: Does it require event sourcing?
faq.answer: No. It supports event-sourced designs, but CQRS can also use simpler synchronization patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate production code?
faq.answer: It provides templates and architecture guidance. You must adapt implementation details to your stack and operational needs.

faq.question: When should I avoid CQRS?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the domain is simple, CRUD is enough, or immediate consistency is required everywhere.

faq.question: Does it cover API design?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows command and query endpoint separation using FastAPI-style examples.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
